newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian financial system 9-mo profits drop 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombian financial system 9-mo profits drop 8 pct.

text.p: The Colombian financial system saw its accumulated nine-month net profits to September tumble 8.0 percent to 483 billion pesos, the country's banking superintendency said Wednesday.
It said banks and other credit institutions had seen profits hit by returns on investment that were lower than in the same period of 1995.
In the 1996 nine months, the financial system's total assets rose 24 percent to 54 trillion pesos, it said.
Banking Superintendent Mara Luisa Chiappe said banks bucked the overall trend, increasing their accumulated nine-month profits by 13 percent, to 335 billion pesos.
Savings banks and building societies saw accumuluated net profits grow 69 percent, to 155 billion pesos.

Banco Ganadero consolidated its position as Colombia's largest bank in terms of assets, which stand at 3.5 trillion pesos. It is followed by Banco de Colombia with total assets of 2.81 trillion pesos, and Bancaf with 2.63 trillion pesos of assets.
Chiappe said unpaid debt in the first nine months of 1996 rose 53 percent from a year earlier, to 2.5 trillion pesos. He said the financial sector remained "highly solvent."
